research_question: In adults undergoing cardiac surgery via sternotomy, does an implantable gentamicin-collagen sponge placed in the sternal wound at closure, compared with no topical antimicrobial, reduce the incidence of superficial surgical site infection?
treatment_label: Gentamicin-collagen sponge (gentamicin-impregnated collagen implant) in the sternotomy wound
control_label: No topical antimicrobial (standard wound closure / placebo / usual care)
outcome_description: Incidence of SUPERFICIAL surgical site infection of the sternotomy wound (events / total randomized per arm), as defined by CDC criteria or the trial's own definition of superficial sternal wound infection. Deep sternal wound infection/mediastinitis and combined total SSI figures are not the target of this analysis.
positive_direction: A positive Hedges g (or RR < 1 on the risk-ratio scale) means the gentamicin-collagen sponge group had FEWER superficial surgical site infections than the no-topical-antimicrobial control group — i.e. the sponge reduced superficial SSI.
search_queries: gentamicin collagen sponge sternotomy sternal wound infection randomized trial
gentamicin-impregnated collagen implant cardiac surgery surgical site infection controlled trial
topical gentamicin sponge coronary artery bypass sternal wound infection outcome
inclusion_criteria: Adults undergoing cardiac surgery via median sternotomy (any procedure type, e.g. CABG, valve, combined)
Study evaluates a locally implanted gentamicin-collagen sponge/implant in the sternal wound compared with a group not receiving a topical antimicrobial
Reports quantitative data on surgical site / sternal wound infection, including superficial infection counts or data from which they can be derived
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, opinion piece, narrative review, theoretical or protocol-only paper)
No comparison group — single-arm or purely descriptive cohort with no control condition receiving no topical antimicrobial
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (no event counts/proportions, means+SDs, t/F values, or odds/risk ratios)

Completely unrelated to the topic (non-cardiac/non-sternotomy surgery, non-gentamicin local agent only, systemic antibiotic prophylaxis or antiseptic wash comparisons only, animal or in vitro studies)
moderators_to_extract: Number of sponges and gentamicin dose (e.g. 130 mg vs 260 mg)
Diabetes prevalence / proportion of high-risk patients
Definition and ascertainment of SSI (CDC criteria vs trial-specific) and follow-up duration
Sample size category and risk-of-bias / blinding status
effect_size_note: Dichotomous outcome: pool as Risk Ratio using superficial SSI events and total randomized per arm, random-effects (DerSimonian-Laird or REML) with continuity correction for zero-event arms as needed; RR < 1 favors the gentamicin-collagen sponge. Deep SSI is analyzed separately in the same review.
